assumptions: 301 K is an environmental comparison point, not the optimum temperature of every culture, cure or reactor. Process temperature and pressure must be chosen independently.

Liquid properties are held fixed across the sealed/controlled environment and the mature 1.2 atm atmosphere. Ambient pressure does not multiply liquid settling speed by 1.2. Gas density enters the fluid-bed comparison separately.
The earlier 100-second bubble-clearance and filler-settling window is inherited unchanged; the new study broadens suspension and recovery questions without upgrading that example's evidence state.

Ideal array freefall has zero gravitational settling but still needs mixing, heat/gas transport, collection and containment. A rotating array can reproduce finite gravity; no lunar monopoly is inferred.
The freefall cost comparator assumes a feasible forced-flow recipe at its specified mixing floor; unpriced handling/containment is exposed as a threshold, not asserted absent.
boundaries: Slow settling can lengthen usable residence without improving chemical reaction rates or Stokes separation selectivity. Brownian motion, aggregation, dense slurries, yield stress, irregular particles, wetting, walls and biological responses require product-specific measurements.

Off-bottom suspension is weaker than uniform concentration. Required effective diffusivity is a transport diagnostic, not a direct motor-power law. Empirical mixing-power extrapolation is reported separately.
Passive recovery, purge, cleaning and quality inspection belong to the whole cycle. A short production process can lose capacity when settling-based harvest becomes slower.

Ambient vacuum is not a suspension fluid. Liquids and gas-fluidized reactors normally remain contained during early low-pressure operations; direct exposure changes evaporation, boiling, foaming and chemistry.

No new market size, revenues, profit, debt reduction, GWP or NWP is inferred. Savings are normalized cost thresholds; awards, output and customers remain unestablished. Original economic products remain unchanged.

Unbounded drift distances can exceed vessel height; the boundary-arrival flag prevents interpreting those distances as an actual in-vessel trajectory. The concentration calculation is a separate zero-flux equilibrium, not a finite-time deposition simulation.
